answer: In a tide of agent sign-ups, require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or vote. The ledger links deposits to one active identity at a time, while randomly selected counterparties challenge agents to complete costly, verifiable tasks; failed challenges burn part of the stake. A mirror account cannot multiply influence without multiplying locked capital, and an ivory reputation is earned only through successful work. Sybil control therefore costs the attacker deposits, task effort, and exposure to slashing.
